headline: What 19 IPL seasons say about who qualifies and who wins
intro: I tested 61 measures across batting, bowling and squad shape against three outcomes: league win rate, a playoff place and the title. These are the results that held up, and the ones that did not.

items.label: How much a team's strength repeats from one season to the next
items.body: Across 145 pairs of consecutive seasons, a great year says almost nothing about the next one. Records are context, not forecasts. That is why StatEdge reports ranges and chances, never certainties.

items.label: Wickets are the strongest single marker of a playoff team
items.body: Pick one playoff team and one non-playoff team at random: 78% of the time the playoff team took wickets faster. Losing wickets slowly with the bat points the same way (77%).

items.label: Champions that also finished top two on league win rate
items.body: Six did not. The title adds real luck on top of strength, so even the best squad should be priced as a favourite, not a certainty.

items.label: A settled XI goes with qualifying
items.body: Teams that used fewer players across a season qualified more often (76% in the same pairwise sense). Part of that is cause and part is effect, since winning sides rotate less, so it is a risk flag and not a lever.

items.label: The toss and season success
items.body: A weak link between winning more tosses and winning more games. The toss shapes single matches, but it does not decide seasons.

items.label: Qualifiers lean on their top three batters
items.body: Playoff teams gave more of their balls to their top three than non-qualifiers did (76% pairwise). Concentration helps, until one early wicket decides the innings.

learned.title: Strike rate and dot balls matter, but they are not extra signals
learned.body: Runs per over, boundary rate and dot-ball rate each track winning. Once you account for runs scored and wickets lost in each phase, they add almost nothing. Counting them again would double-count the same performance.

learned.title: Death-over extras are a hidden cost
learned.body: Wides and no-balls in overs 16 to 20 cost teams more than their run value. It is one of the few things that cost winning beyond what runs and wickets already show.

learned.title: All-rounders, bowling depth and star reliance did not stand out
learned.body: None showed a reliable link to success beyond runs and wickets. That does not make them useless; it means this data cannot prove it.

learned.title: With 61 measures, a few look important by chance
learned.body: About three would pass a 95% test by luck alone. I treat single passes as leads and look for the same direction in the early and recent years before trusting one.
